findings.title: English <noscript> text left under lang="es"
findings.description: The page now declares `<html lang="es">`, but `<noscript>Please enable JavaScript to continue using this application.</noscript>` is still English. Visitors without JavaScript see English, and screen readers read it with Spanish pronunciation. It is the last Angular scaffold leftover in the file; the PR's purpose (US2, SC-003) is for the page to present itself in Spanish.

A.approach: Translate it: `<noscript>Activa JavaScript para usar esta aplicación.</noscript>`, and note it in the spec (FR-001 / Project Structure).
A.rationale: Completes the lang change with a one-line, zero-risk edit.

B.approach: Keep the English text and mark it `lang="en"`.
B.rationale: Metadata correct, but visitors still read English.

C.approach: Leave it and record a follow-up.
C.rationale: No diff change, visible inconsistency stays.

findings.title: Archive says mozjpeg; the built JPEG is baseline without the mozjpeg preset
findings.description: Spec Technical Summary, plan.md (Research Findings, W0) and T001 say "JPEG with mozjpeg, quality about 85". `file src/assets/link_preview.jpg` reports baseline: sharp's mozjpeg preset forces progressive output, so it was dropped. The archive is the only record of how the asset was produced. FR-006/FR-007 don't require mozjpeg, so this is wording, not non-compliance.

A.approach: Reword spec.md, plan.md and tasks.json (re-render tasks.md) to "sharp JPEG q85, baseline (no mozjpeg preset, which forces progressive), optimised Huffman + trellis, metadata stripped"; mirror on the issue's spec/plan comments.
A.rationale: Archive matches the artifact and records why.

B.approach: Keep the plan text and add a Deviations note.
B.rationale: Documents the delta but leaves contradictory statements.
